title: Record-Triggered Automation: Row-Level Rejection in a Nightly Bulk Load

steps.prompt: A nightly integration upserts 200,000 Invoice__c records. Each invoice's discount is calculated from rows in 5 child objects, and an invoice whose calculation fails must be rejected from the load while the other invoices save. Which automation should the architect build?

options.label: Record-triggered flow whose asynchronous path computes discounts from the child objects
options.rationale: The asynchronous path runs in a separate transaction after the invoices commit, so a failed calculation can no longer reject its invoice from the load.

options.label: Bulkified Apex trigger that calls addError on each failing invoice
options.rationale: For complex, high-volume record logic the record-triggered guide favors Apex, which gives the control Flow trades for simplicity. An error raised inside the save lets the platform's partial save drop only the failing invoices and commit the rest.

options.label: Scheduled Batch Apex job that recalculates discounts after the load ends
options.rationale: A job that starts after the load sees invoices that are already saved, so a failed calculation cannot keep its invoice out of the load.
